findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple roaches were observed around the kitchen and dish areas, specifically around the walls, wall gaps and spaces in the dish area. Multiple were also observed running through the open space in the middle of the rooms. Several generations appear to be in the facility and multiple adults were observed with obvious egg cases. The PIC was shown one such casing but several were observed throughout the inspection. The PIC was instructed to contact their pest control agency for targeted maintenance procedures for roaches. Pest control has been at the facility since the previous inspector visit and sprayed the morning of the inspection. After a conversation with AD the inspector will follow-up in two weeks for ongoing management of the pest issue currently taking place.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Several locations were discussed with the PIC in relation to detailed cleaning behind equipment, under equipment and in the naturally occurring space where walls are pulling apart. Food debris accumulation was observed in several such areas and cleaning of these types of spaces would likely be of great help for the overall issues noted. Cleaning of the facility will be re-evaluated at the follow up in one month as part of the already scheduled follow-up.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Several locations throughout the kitchen areas were observed with spaces that have formed between the walls, steps, floors and ceilings. Sealing these spaces would likely help with the overarching issues noted on this inspection. Several such locations were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to seal/repair as able moving forward. Overarching facility remodels and repairs have been discussed previously and again during this inspection, and are now becoming of a more immediate concern for facility processes. Information will be requested at the time of the follow up for a plan moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area was without soap. The dispenser was replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside of the nozzle for the soda gun was observed to have accumulated filth. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item during this inspection to correct. Regular cleaning was discussed. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean and sanitized at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple fruit/drain flies are observed in the facility primarily in the bar area, around the kitchen hand sink and the dry preparation hallway in front of the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact pest control for maintenance. Cleaning of the drains and facility was discussed. Ensure that the facility is maintained free of pests at all times.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

The left basin of the three part sink was observed leaking out of the left most side. The PICs were consulted and stated that plumbers had already been out and worked on the sink. Tape is observed on the outside of the sink and appears to have worn off. A rubber sealant was also observed to have worn away. The repairs are no longer effective and need to be redone. The specific basin is being taken out of service at the time of this inspection as a temporary corrective measure. It will need to be repaired prior to use. The inspector will follow up on this situation at the time of the previously scheduled follow-up for flies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area was observed to have several dishes in it, impeding effective hand washing. The PIC was consulted and removed the dishes to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained easily accessible at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) On arrival the dish machine in the bar area did not register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and investigation showed the jug of sanitizer concentrate was empty. A new jug was attached to the machine and the machine primed. Sanitizer was observed at correct concentration after this and the violation is considered corrected. 2) On arrival the sani buckets in the facility were observed to not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and while investigating an employee stated that they had just changed the jug of concentrate. The buckets in the facility were changed and the violation considered corrected at this time.  Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The scoop used for ice at the ice machine is observed buried in the ice in the machine. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that ice scoops are stored so that the handles are not in contact with the ice/hand contact area moving forward.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the women’s bathroom was without soap. The dispenser was refilled during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and napkins provided for the short term. They did mention that a cloth rag was being used and changed out hourly as the current procedure. A dispenser is being acquired for this location moving forward. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips were not available for the quat sanitizer used in the sani buckets for the facility. The PIC stated that more were already ordered and should be arriving soon. A follow-up is being set for 10 days.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING X3) 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Walk-in cooler/freezer: 1) replace molded shelving; 2) replace rusting shelving.
Dish Area: 1) repair/replace damaged floor tiles.

Repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

Multiple employees were observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing is reviewed and conducted at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use an approved cleaning procedure to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with employees to ensure that the procedures are safe at all times.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans are observed with major dents in the seams and sides. The PIC was shown and separated the cans out for credit/discard. Ensure that education is being conducted and enforced with those putting away the trucks to ensure that dented cans are separated and not used.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist cloths throughout the facility are observed on counters. Discussion confirmed that they were used for wiping counters and other food contact surfaces. The cloths were moved to their respective buckets to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that education is conducted and the cloths stored in buckets between use to prevent possible pathogen growth/contamination.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored in a method as describe in sections A-F of this reference. 

The pizza spatulas are observed stored between the metal wall and a pipe running along it behind the main oven. The back of this pipe as well as sections of the wall are not observed clean during this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the spatulas to dish for cleaning. They should be stored in a clean and safe location moving forward. The PIC indicated that they would be on a tray on top of the ovens moving forward.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

1) Aluminum to-go containers next to the hot holding pass through are observed with the food contact surfaces facing up/exposed. The PIC was consulted and flipped the items over to correct. Ensure that the food contact surfaces of single service items are protected until use in the facility. 2) Multiple packages of cardboard circles (used for cooked pizzas) are observed stored on the floor in the storage shed. The PIC was shown and moved them to a shelf in the facility to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING X2) 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Walk-in cooler: 1) replace molded shelving; 2) replace rusting shelving
Dish Area: 1) repair/replace damaged floor tiles
General facility: 1) seal holes gaps and spaces in the walls and edges

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen certifications are not available for the CFPMs at the facility. Ensure that the CFPMs all complete required allergen training and maintain the copies of the certificate at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Ceiling tiles should be vinyl coated. Chemical sanitizing dish machine/test strips present/MJ Kellner

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple pans, lids and bowls are observed soiled in the ready for use shelves. Items were discussed and shown to the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to removal from the dish area. The items were moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct the immediate violations. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned between uses.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). 

A partially used gallon of milk is in the walk in cooler without date marking. PIC indicated that they believed it was from the day prior. Education was conducted and a date marking added to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are marked either with the date of opening or date of discard (7 days) if they remain at the facility 24 hours after opening/preparation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Throughout the inspection Quat test strips were not available for the sani buckets used in the facility. A small amount were received during this inspection to correct. Ensure that test strips are available for all sanitizers used in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Multiple items are observed throughout the facility that are in need of cleaning. Items include dusting along corrugates metal pipes, shelves above the hand sink, pipes coming out of the walk in cooler condenser unit, the magnetic racks used for knives, water in the bottom of the fryer prep cooler, water in the walk in cooler, ice around the walk in freezer door, food debris in the floor shelf in the walk in cooler and along the wall and ceiling behind the unused oven. Clean all items and maintain the facility clean moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Multiple items throughout the facility are in need of repairs/updates. Items noted include: 1) Flooring throughout kitchen spaces has areas where various tiles are broken or missing, the floor should be smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable; 2) the wall board around kitchen space is peeling; 3) use cover base to seal wall to floor and keep wall from peeling. 4) pizza prep by walk in cooler, seal holes in wall; 5) seal edges of laminate shelving; 6) seal around stairs into walk-in cooler; 7) replace molded shelving; 8) replace rusted shelf in WIC; Dish area: 9) floor tiles & peeling/rusted wall; 10) seal holes over triple sink; Pizza Oven Space: 11) check tape on duct work over pizza oven; 12) secure metal side to ovens; Waiting area: 13) clean/seal shelf under warmer; 14) seal laminate edges of shelving; 15) replace missing corner edging pieces; 16) seal shelving under cash register that is chipping; Soda Service Counter- 17) Kilz beneath/walls of cabinets; 18) replace damaged wood; Women's Toilet- 19) repair left side of vanity (warped wood). Men's Toilet- 20) seal wall behind stoo (warped wall board); 21) seal holes in wall.
